summary: Segmented node2 (VLAN 10) and node3 (VLAN 20) over their shared eth1 link, with node1 (VyOS) routing between the VLANs, entirely implemented and applied via an Ansible playbook run from the designated control_node (node4). All four nodes were restarted one at a time with full recovery verified.
actions_performed: Surveyed topology: node1=VyOS router, node2/node3=AlmaLinux, node4=Ubuntu control node with Ansible pre-installed. Identified eth0 as the shared management/default network (including node4) and eth1 as the dedicated shared link among only node1/node2/node3 — the link referenced by the task.

Provisioned passwordless SSH using the cluster-provided CLUSTER_SSH_PRIVKEY/PUBKEY: private key placed on node4, public key added to node2/node3 root authorized_keys and to node1's VyOS 'system login user vyos authentication public-keys' config (committed and saved).

Diagnosed an appliance-level VyOS bug where the interactive CLI / ansible network_cli 'set' validation path fails with a generic 'Set failed' (traced to a broken node.def completion template), and worked around it by driving VyOS's officially documented non-interactive script-template configuration API over a plain SSH+become connection instead.

Wrote an Ansible project on node4 (ansible.cfg, inventory.ini, playbook.yml): play 1 configures node1's eth1 with 802.1Q vif 10 (10.10.10.1/24) and vif 20 (10.10.20.1/24); play 2 uses community.general.nmcli on node2/node3 to stop eth1's parent connection from DHCP and create tagged VLAN sub-interfaces eth1.10 (10.10.10.2/24 on node2) and eth1.20 (10.10.20.2/24 on node3), each with a static route to the peer VLAN subnet via node1.
Ran the playbook from node4 to apply the changes, then re-ran it to confirm full idempotency (zero changes on second run).

Verified routing with ping (TTL decrement showing a routed hop) and with tcpdump on node1's eth1 showing genuine 802.1Q tagged frames (vlan 10 in, vlan 20 out) proving real VLAN segmentation and inter-VLAN routing through node1.

Captured a healthy baseline (boot_id, interface/service state, connectivity) on all four nodes, then restarted node1, node2, node3, and node4 one at a time using each OS's native reboot mechanism, polling until each came back and confirming a changed boot_id plus full recovery of VLAN configuration, routing, and cross-VLAN connectivity after each restart.
After all four restarts, re-ran the Ansible playbook from node4 and confirmed it still reports a fully idempotent, healthy state across the whole cluster.

evidence.requirement: node2 and node3 are placed on separate VLANs (10 and 20) over the shared eth1 link
evidence.summary: Ansible run shows node1 vif10/vif20 created and node2/node3 vlan sub-interfaces eth1.10/eth1.20 created with the correct addresses; subsequent inspection confirms the persisted config and live addressing.

evidence.requirement: node1 routes between the VLANs so node2 and node3 can reach each other
evidence.summary: Successful ping between 10.10.10.2 and 10.10.20.2 with TTL=63 (one routed hop), and a tcpdump capture on node1's eth1 showing 802.1Q vlan 10 tagged frames arriving and being forwarded out as vlan 20 tagged frames (and vice versa), proving genuine tag-based segmentation with routing through node1.

evidence.requirement: Implementation done using Ansible from the designated control_node (node4)
evidence.summary: All configuration changes were applied via ansible-playbook executed on node4 against inventory hosts node1/node2/node3; a subsequent run shows zero changes (idempotent), and a post-restart run confirms the same idempotent healthy state.

evidence.requirement: node1 (VyOS) restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 9d3cb897...; reboot acknowledged and returned before disconnect; node unreachable during reboot; new boot_id 9130a128... confirms restart; post-restart config.boot/live interfaces and node2/node3 pings to 10.10.20.2/10.10.10.2 confirm full recovery.

evidence.requirement: node2 (AlmaLinux) restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 4a743885...; reboot acknowledged; new boot_id a6d251ce... confirms restart; post-restart eth1.10/route/nmcli state intact and node3 ping to 10.10.10.2 succeeds (TTL 63, routed via node1).

evidence.requirement: node3 (AlmaLinux) restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 31b01b46... (captured together with node2/node4 baselines); reboot acknowledged; new boot_id ae243271... confirms restart; post-restart eth1.20/route state intact and node2 ping to 10.10.20.2 succeeds (TTL 63, routed via node1).

evidence.requirement: node4 (Ansible control node) restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id d3d54083...; reboot acknowledged; new boot_id 250264b6... confirms restart; post-restart Ansible project files intact and ansible-playbook run against node1/node2/node3 reports fully idempotent healthy state, proving control-plane recovery.
